lesson_title: A Scar Two Billion Years Old
hook_text: Drive to Parys in the Free State and you are standing inside the largest asteroid impact structure on Earth.
clip_script: Two billion years ago, a space rock perhaps ten kilometres across slammed into what is now the Free State. The ring of hills around Parys, the Vredefort Dome, is all that is left. That rock was one of the Sun's huge family. Eight planets: small rocky Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars, then the giants Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune. Moons by the hundred, some with hidden oceans. Millions of asteroids between Mars and Jupiter, rocky leftovers that never became a planet. Dwarf planets like Ceres and Pluto, round but sharing their orbits with crowds of other objects. Beyond Neptune, the icy Kuiper Belt, and far beyond that the Oort Cloud, where comets wait. When one falls towards the Sun, it grows a glowing tail that always points away from the Sun. And every shooting star you see is a tiny piece of this family burning up in our sky.
visual_style: A whiteboard aerial view of the Vredefort ring of hills, zooming out to a map of the Solar System with planets, the asteroid belt, the Kuiper Belt, the Oort Cloud and a comet with its tail.
pacing: A dramatic local hook, then a sweeping zoom outward.
